script.title: Why Taiwan's Engineers Put Green Snack Bags on Servers
sentences: Taiwanese engineers leave bags of corn puffs on their servers.
The snack is called Kuai Kuai, and it also sits on ATMs and toll booths.
The bag must be green, never expired, and nobody may open it.
In May 2017, Taiwan's Ministry of Finance tried it on its overloaded tax systems.
They bought yellow bags, and people online criticized them for it.
Kuai Kuai means obedient, and green matches the light that says a machine works fine.
One ride maker, Brogent Technologies, writes exactly how to place the bags into its contracts.
script.description:
In Taiwan, a green bag of Kuai Kuai snacks sits on servers, ATMs and toll booths.
The name means obedient, and the color matters.
claims_en: People in Taiwan put Kuai Kuai puff corn snacks next to or on top of machines, including in server rooms.
Kuai Kuai is also placed next to ATMs and toll booths.
There is a rigid set of practices: green bags only, not expired, and no one may open and eat them.
In May 2017 the Ministry of Finance tried to place Kuai Kuai to help its operational systems overwhelmed by overload during tax collection.
They bought yellow bags, drawing criticism from netizens in Taiwan.
Kuai Kuai stands for obedient or well-behaved.
The green bag matches the green indicator light denoting correct function.
Brogent Technologies requires its gaming equipment outside Taiwan to be adorned with Kuai Kuai, with the precise manner written in its contracts.
